What comes up in The Entrance

3 conditions, and each one is handled differently

Every site is scoped on the day. What follows is how this work normally runs in the area, not a reading of any one block.

Knockdown on a tight beachside block

The standard job here, where access decides the method before the structure does.

How it is handled
Smaller plant or hand work, with material carried out to the kerb and loaded in sequenced loads.
What does it
Mini excavator, hand tools, bogie or 10 wheeler tippers.

Weathered fibro on older stock

Eaves, roofing and wall sheeting that have been in the salt air for decades.

How it is handled
Condition assessed before disturbance, because weathered sheeting may have to be handled as friable rather than bonded.
What does it
Licensed asbestos removalists, licence class set by the condition.

Freestanding houses

Single and double storey brick, brick veneer, fibro and timber. The era matters more than the material, because anything built before 1990 carries a hazardous materials assumption until it is tested.

How it is handled
Hazardous materials removed and cleared first, services disconnected in writing, then the structure taken down and the material separated as it falls.
What does it
Excavator with a demolition grapple, sized to the side access rather than to the house. Zero tail swing where the work runs hard against a boundary.

The Entrance

What shapes the work on these blocks

  • Dense holiday and permanent housing Close together on small blocks with little side access.
  • Narrow streets Where a truck and dog frequently cannot stand or turn at all.
  • Older fibro stock Much of it pre 1990 and weathered by the coastal exposure.
  • Unit and townhouse redevelopment Around the centre, which brings multi dwelling work alongside knockdowns.

The Entrance has the tightest streets on this part of the coast. Material goes out in smaller vehicles sequenced against the machine, and where a side gap will not take a machine the work goes to hand demolition with material carried out.

The Entrance questions

What people ask before we start

Why does the street matter so much here?
Because it decides the number of loads. A street that will not take a truck and dog turns the same volume into far more tipper movements, which is a longer programme and a different price.
Can you demolish one unit of a block without touching the rest?
That is partial demolition and it is specialist work. The retained structure is propped and supported, the junction is detailed and made weatherproof, and the demolition at the boundary is done by hand.
Does sandy ground change how an excavation is done?
Yes. Sandy material drains well and batters poorly, so a face that has to stand is battered back or supported rather than left vertical, and near the water the water table is close enough that dewatering is planned rather than discovered.
Who actually removes the asbestos?
Licensed asbestos removalists do the removal. Max holds demolition licence AD214737 and builds the programme around them, and an independent licensed assessor handles the air monitoring and the clearance. You are dealing with one contract rather than three.
